unit.title: Shots and Paddle Talk
unit.summary: The shot vocabulary: dinks, drops, drives, volleys, lobs, and flashy shots like Ernes and ATPs. Grip, stance and slang.

lessons.title: Dink, drop, drive
lessons.objective: Name the three core shots by flight and purpose.

payload.prompt: Match each shot to its description.

pairs.definition: A soft shot that lands in the opponent's kitchen; the foundation of patient pickleball.
A soft arcing shot from further back that lands low in the kitchen.
A hard, flat, fast shot meant to put pressure on the opponent or end the rally.

distractorDefinitions: A spinning shot that bounces high

explanation.summary: Dinks are the bread and butter; drops buy time from the baseline; drives attack.
explanation.sayThisLine: Dink is soft at the net, drop is an arc from back, drive is hard and flat.

payload.prompt: What is a dink in pickleball?

options.text: A soft shot that lands in the opponent's kitchen
A hard shot hit at the net
A shot that touches the net cord

explanation.correct: A dink is soft and controlled, landing in the opponent's kitchen. It's the foundation of a patient game.
explanation.incorrect: Dinks are the soft shots at the net, not hard or fast. Dinking is how you win through patience.
explanation.sayThisLine: Dink soft into the kitchen, the heart of pickleball.

payload.prompt: From the baseline you float a soft arc that lands in their kitchen. A drop?

scene.alt: Baseline scenario: a soft, arcing shot from the back of the court that lands in the opponents' kitchen.

explanation.correct: Yes. A drop is a soft arc from the back of the court that lands low in the opponents' kitchen, which gives your team time to move forward.
explanation.incorrect: That is what a drop is: a soft, arcing shot from the back that lands gently in the kitchen. A dink is the same idea hit from up near the kitchen.
explanation.sayThisLine: Drop shot: soft arc from back, lands in the kitchen.

payload.prompt: A dink pops up above net height. What do you hit?

situation.narrative: During a dink rally, your opponent's dink floats up a little higher than the net, right in front of you.

options.label: A drive: hit it flat and hard
options.consequence: Good read. A ball that sits up above the net can be hit down, so a firm, flat shot is the natural way to take the point.
considerations: The ball is attackable above net height
You can hit down on it
Aim away from the opponents if you can

options.label: Another dink back into the kitchen
options.consequence: Safe, but you pass up the chance. A high dink is exactly the ball players wait for.
considerations: Gives the opponent a fresh chance
Better saved for balls below net height

payload.expertNote: Spotting a ball you can hit down on is the heart of the dink game. Below the net you dink; above it you can attack.

statement.speaker: Sam
statement.text: We were just dinking back and forth forever. It was boring.

payload.question: What should you say?

options.text: Dink wars can go on forever! Who finally blinked?
Dinking is the whole point. You were doing it wrong.

payload.translation: Sam is describing a dink war: a long rally of soft shots at the kitchen where nobody wants to be the first to pop the ball up.

followUps.line: Ha, a dink war! Who finally popped one up?
followUps.why: Shows you know the term and asks a curious question.

followUps.line: I'm still learning, but I think that's the point: the first person to pop one up usually loses it.
followUps.why: Offers your understanding honestly, without claiming expertise.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Sam said it was boring. You do not need to defend dinking. Curiosity about how it ended is a warmer reply than a lecture.

lessons.title: Volley, block, overhead
lessons.objective: Tell volleys, blocks and smashes apart.

payload.prompt: Match each shot to its meaning.

pairs.definition: Hitting the ball before it bounces on the court, usually at the net.
A compact, absorbing volley that returns a fast ball softly into the kitchen.
An aggressive shot hit from above your head, used on lobs and high balls.

distractorDefinitions: A shot you hit only after letting the ball bounce

explanation.summary: Volleys are any unbounced hit at the net; blocks soften fast balls; overheads finish lobs.
explanation.sayThisLine: Volley is any unbounced hit; block is a soft absorb; overhead is an aggressive smash.

payload.prompt: Complete the description of a block.
payload.template: A block is a short {{shot-type}} that {{action}} the pace of a hard ball.

explanation.correct: A block is a short, compact volley that soaks up the pace of a hard ball and sends it back low and soft.
explanation.incorrect: A block is not a lob and does not add power. You hold the paddle firm and let the ball's own speed do the work.
explanation.sayThisLine: A block is a short volley that soaks up the pace.

payload.prompt: A high lob comes at you and you hit it hard from above your head. A smash?

scene.alt: Scenario: a high lob drops toward you and you swing down through it from above your head.

explanation.correct: Yes, hitting a high ball aggressively from overhead is the definition of a smash.
explanation.incorrect: A smash is exactly that: an aggressive overhead hit, usually on a lob.
explanation.sayThisLine: Overhead smash: high ball, hit hard from above your head.

payload.prompt: Your opponent drives a hard ball at your feet at the net. You don't have time for a full swing. What do you hit?

options.text: A block: absorb the pace and return it softly

explanation.correct: A block is perfect here: compact, absorbing the pace of the incoming ball and returning it gently.
explanation.incorrect: You don't have time for a smash or another drive. A block absorbs fast balls with minimal swing.
explanation.sayThisLine: Block is a short, compact volley that softens a hard ball.

payload.prompt: Match each showy shot to its definition.

pairs.definition: A high shot over the opponents' heads, either defensive or offensive.
A shot that goes around the outside of the net post instead of over the net, then lands in the court.
A volley hit from outside the kitchen after a leap around its corner near the post. Named after player Erne Perry.
An Erne-style shot from the far side: you run behind your partner to volley from their side of the court.

distractorDefinitions: A soft arc from the back that lands in the kitchen
A serve struck from above the waist

explanation.summary: These are the flashy ones: a lob over their heads, an ATP around the post, an Erne outside the kitchen, and a Bert, which is an Erne-style shot from your partner's side.
explanation.sayThisLine: Lob over heads, ATP around the post, Erne outside the kitchen, and Bert is an Erne from your partner's side.

payload.prompt: Leap outside kitchen to volley near post. What's this shot?

image.alt: Player outside the kitchen line, leaping to volley near the net post

explanation.correct: An Erne is a volley hit from outside the kitchen, near the net post, often after a leap around the kitchen corner. The player never touches the kitchen, so it is legal.
explanation.incorrect: A block is a soft, compact volley and a drop is a soft arc from the back. The one with the leap to the post is the Erne.
explanation.sayThisLine: An Erne is a leap around the kitchen to volley at the post.

payload.prompt: The opponents are crowding the net. You hit a high lob over their heads. Why might this work?

options.text: They're vulnerable at the net and have to retreat to reach it
It's an easy shot to hit

explanation.correct: A lob over players at the net forces them to turn and run back, which can win the point or break up their control of the net.
explanation.incorrect: A lob is not automatically a winner and it is not worth extra points. Its job is to send net players backwards, and a short lob just invites a smash.
explanation.sayThisLine: A lob over their heads can send them back from the net.

payload.prompt: A wide ball pulls you off court. Can you go around the net post?

situation.narrative: You are dragged wide beside the net post. Hitting the ball back around the outside of the post, instead of over the net, is tempting.

facts.label: Where you are
facts.value: Wide of the court, beside the net post

facts.label: The idea
facts.value: Hit it around the post, not over the net

options.label: Yes, an ATP is allowed if the ball lands in the court
options.consequence: Correct. The ball does not have to go over the net, as long as it passes outside the post and lands in bounds. It is hard to pull off, which is why it is a crowd-pleaser.
considerations: Passing outside the post is allowed
It still has to land in the opponents' court
It is tricky, so it is rare

options.label: No, every shot has to go over the net
options.consequence: Not quite. Going around the post is allowed in pickleball, provided the ball lands in the court.
considerations: An ATP is not a fault
What matters is where the ball lands
It needs a wide, awkward ball to set it up

payload.expertNote: ATP means around the post. It is allowed, and it is rare because you need a wide ball and a steady touch to land it.

payload.prompt: What is the difference between topspin and backspin?

options.text: Topspin makes the ball dip down, backspin makes it float or slice
Topspin is slower, backspin is faster

explanation.correct: Topspin rotates forward (making the ball dip), backspin (slice) rotates backward (making it float).
explanation.incorrect: Topspin and backspin are opposite rotations with opposite effects on the ball's flight.
explanation.sayThisLine: Topspin dips down, backspin floats or slices.

payload.prompt: Match each spin to how the ball behaves.

pairs.definition: Forward spin that pulls the ball down, so it dips and kicks forward off the bounce
Backward spin that holds the ball up, so it floats and bounces low
Little or no spin, so the ball just follows its natural arc

distractorDefinitions: Spin that makes the ball stop dead in the air
A spin only allowed on serves

explanation.summary: Topspin dips, backspin floats, and flat has no spin to speak of. You cannot reliably hear spin from the stands, so watch the ball's flight and bounce instead.
explanation.sayThisLine: Topspin dips, backspin floats, flat is just flat.

payload.prompt: Complete the spin description.
payload.template: {{spin-type}} makes the ball {{effect}}, while the other makes it {{other-effect}}.

explanation.correct: Topspin dips, backspin floats. They're opposite rotations with opposite effects.
explanation.incorrect: Remember: topspin forward = dip down; backspin backward = float or slice.
explanation.sayThisLine: Topspin dips, backspin floats.

payload.prompt: Does topspin make a ball dip down, or float up?

scene.alt: Shot scenario: a ball hit with topspin crosses the net and drops.

explanation.correct: Topspin spins the ball forward, which pulls it down so it drops sooner than a flat ball. That lets players hit harder and still land it in.
explanation.incorrect: Floating is what backspin does. Topspin's forward rotation pulls the ball down, so it dips.
explanation.sayThisLine: Topspin pulls the ball down, so it dips.

lessons.title: Grip, ready, split
lessons.objective: Recognise the ready position and split step.

payload.prompt: Tap as opponent contacts the ball: split-step timing.

explanation.correct: A split step is that small hop right as the opponent swings, pushing you ready to react.
explanation.incorrect: Split step timing is critical: too early or late and you lose reactivity.
explanation.sayThisLine: Split step as they hit, so you're ready to move.

payload.prompt: Put one exchange in order, from your shot to your next move.

items.why: Every exchange starts with your own contact.

items.text: You recover to the ready position, paddle up
items.why: Knees bent and paddle in front get you set for the next ball.

items.text: You split step as your opponent hits
items.why: The small hop is timed to their contact so you can push off.

items.text: You push off toward the ball
items.why: You see where the ball is going, then move to it.

explanation.correct: Hit, recover to ready, split step as they hit, then push off toward the ball. It repeats on every shot.
explanation.incorrect: The ready position comes after your own shot and before their contact. The split step follows it, and the move comes last.
explanation.sayThisLine: Hit, get ready, split step, go.

payload.prompt: What is a continental grip?

options.text: Holding the paddle like a hammer, neutral for most shots

explanation.correct: Continental grip is the neutral hammer-like hold, versatile for volleys, drives and dinks.
explanation.incorrect: Continental is the neutral, versatile grip that works for many shots.
explanation.sayThisLine: Continental grip: hold it like a hammer.

payload.prompt: You're at the kitchen line, opponent is about to swing. Do you split step before or after they hit?

scene.alt: Net scenario: opponent about to swing.

explanation.correct: A split step is a small hop timed to their contact, so you land ready to push off in any direction.
explanation.incorrect: Hopping after they hit is too late, because the ball is already on its way. The hop goes at their contact, like a loaded spring.
explanation.sayThisLine: Split step as they hit the ball.

payload.prompt: Listen to this shot sound. What type?

audio.description: Soft, quiet sound of a dink shot at the net

explanation.correct: That soft, quiet pop is a dink. The ball touches the paddle gently.
explanation.incorrect: Dinks have a quiet, controlled sound. Drives are loud and sharp.
explanation.sayThisLine: Dink sound: soft. Drive sound: loud and sharp.

payload.prompt: What does the sound tell you about a dink vs a drive?

options.text: Dinks are quiet and controlled; drives are loud and sharp

explanation.correct: The paddle-to-ball contact is gentle on a dink (quiet pop), aggressive on a drive (sharp crack).
explanation.incorrect: Sound reflects the shot speed and force. Soft shots sound quiet, hard shots sound loud.
explanation.sayThisLine: Quiet sound is dink, loud crack is drive.

payload.prompt: You hear a sharp, explosive pop. Is this a dink?

explanation.correct: A sharp, explosive sound is a drive or smash, not a quiet dink.
explanation.incorrect: Sharp sounds come from hard shots like drives; dinks are quiet.
explanation.sayThisLine: Sharp pop = drive or smash, not dink.

statement.speaker: Sam
statement.text: I can tell what shot they're hitting just by the sound now.

payload.question: What should you say?

options.text: That's so cool! So dinks are quiet and drives are loud and sharp?
That doesn't make sense, all paddle sounds are the same.

payload.translation: Sam can now hear the difference: soft shots sound quiet, hard shots sound loud and sharp.

followUps.line: So a quiet pop is a dink and a sharp crack is a drive or smash? I want to learn to hear that.
followUps.why: Shows you are curious and learning, not claiming to already hear it.

followUps.line: Teach me? Next time we watch a game, tell me what you hear.
followUps.why: Turns Sam's new skill into something you can share.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: You do not have to hear it yet. Asking Sam to teach you is warmer than pretending.

statement.speaker: Sam
statement.text: We got pickled in game two. 11-0. I'm so mad.

payload.question: What should you say?

options.text: Ouch, 11-0 is rough. Tough matchup, or just an off night?

payload.translation: Getting pickled means losing a game without scoring a point, like 11-0. It stings, so Sam wants sympathy more than advice.

followUps.line: Ouch. Pickled is the worst. Was it a tough matchup, or just an off night?
followUps.why: Shows you know the term and asks a curious, kind question.

followUps.line: That sounds frustrating. Want to tell me about it?

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Being pickled is painful and a little funny. Start with sympathy, and let Sam decide whether to laugh about it.

payload.prompt: Complete the slang descriptions.
payload.template: A {{player-type}} is someone who {{style}}; the opposite plays soft and patient.

explanation.correct: Banger = power player hitting hard; dinker = soft-game player. Both can win.
explanation.incorrect: Bangers hit hard, dinkers play soft. Neither is bad; it's just style.
explanation.sayThisLine: Banger hits hard, dinker plays soft. Both playstyles work.

payload.title: After the game: shot talk
payload.setting: You and Sam are talking after a league night where Sam played two very different opponents.

exchanges.theirMessage: I played a total banger in game one and got smoked.

replies.text: A banger is someone who hits everything hard, right? Did the hard shots backfire?
replies.theirResponse: Yeah, I couldn't settle into a dink rally with him. He just kept driving.
replies.coachNote: You checked the term and asked how the style affected the game.

replies.theirResponse: Someone who hits everything hard. Power player.
replies.coachNote: A perfectly good question, and asking beats pretending. A guess from context would have been a bonus.

replies.text: Bangers are annoying, you should have smashed him back.
replies.theirResponse: He was faster than me. Dismissing his style doesn't help.
replies.coachNote: Do not dunk on a playstyle. Curiosity beats advice.

exchanges.theirMessage: But game two was against a dinker and we had a 15-minute dink rally.

replies.text: Oh wow, a dinker loves the soft game. Did you wear them out or did they win the rally?
replies.theirResponse: They won it. I was the one who popped it up first.
replies.coachNote: You understood the dinker's style and asked the outcome.

replies.theirResponse: It was. But we were in a flow.
replies.coachNote: True, but ask about the strategy or winner.

replies.text: Dinkers are boring. Why didn't you just speed up?
replies.theirResponse: Because they're good at dinking and I kept popping up.
replies.coachNote: Don't mock patience. That's a core skill.

payload.closingNote: A banger hits hard; a dinker plays soft. Both are valid, and good players mix strategies.

payload.prompt: A player who wins by patience and soft dinking is called a dinker. True?

explanation.correct: A dinker plays the soft game and wins through patience and control, not power.
explanation.incorrect: A dinker plays soft; a banger hits hard. Dinkers use patience and strategy.
explanation.sayThisLine: Dinker: soft game and patience. Banger: hard hits.
